From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — Redwood evals & model recommendations

Hi Samira + team,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through your ingestion and QA pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps (TL;DR at the top):

TL;DR: We recommend running a focused eval on the customer-support routing + policy-compliance flows. We'll start with a 1k-example JSONL dataset (sample attached) and run against 3 model families on Redwood: a smaller quantized 7B for throughput (latency baseline), a 13B instruction-tuned quant for balance, and a 33B full-precision variant for quality comparison. See attached prompt set and our evaluation guide.

What we heard:
- Primary use case: automated triage and policy flagging for incoming support tickets (high precision on compliance flags, low false-positive rate).
- Typical input size: 80-180 tokens, with occasional 800+ token threads.
- Main concerns: hallucination on policy citations, PII handling, and consistent classification across regions.

Recommended eval design:
1) Models to test (examples from our catalog):
   - rw-llama-7b-q4: quantized, low-latency baseline
   - rw-llama-13b-q4f: balanced throughput/quality
   - rw-llama-33b: higher-quality reference (fp16)

2) Dataset format (attached sample-eval-dataset.jsonl):
   - JSONL, one example per line with fields: id, input, expected (label or canonical response), meta.source, meta.region
   - For classification tasks, expected is a label; for generation tasks include "expected_text" for exact-match scoring when appropriate.

3) Prompt set (attached fincorp-eval-prompt-set.csv):
   - Includes 8 prompt templates covering short/long context, citation requests, and explicit PII-handling instructions.

4) Scoring criteria and thresholds:
   - Primary metric: F1 on compliance flags (threshold target >= 0.92 for green)
   - Secondary: hallucination rate (measured via citation-accuracy checks) < 5%
   - Latency: 95p token latency target for production <= 350ms for the 7B quantized baseline

Security/ops notes:
- We can run the eval on Redwood Hosted initially using strict data retention (7 days) or on a Dedicated/private instance if you prefer secure egress and KMS integration.
- If you plan to include real customer PII in the eval set, we strongly recommend providing a redacted sample and using our Private eval environment (we can provision a temporary dedicated pool).

Next steps:
1) You: confirm whether you want Hosted vs Dedicated for the eval and share a redacted 200-example sample (or give us permission to stage a secure upload).
2) We: provision the eval job, run baseline models, and return a one-page summary + detailed per-example CSV within 3 business days for a 1k example run.
3) Followup: deep dive with your ML/infra team on any regression cases and tuning.

I've attached the sample dataset, prompt set, and a short Redwood eval guide that describes the JSONL schema and scoring scripts. Neha (CC) will coordinate the actual run if you give the green light.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

--
Attachment stubs: fincorp-eval-prompt-set.csv (CSV, ~8 templates), sample-eval-dataset.jsonl (JSONL sample, 200 rows), redwood-eval-guide.pdf (pdf, 6 pages)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick follow-ups:

1) We prefer Dedicated for this eval because it will include de-identified PII and our security team wants KMS. Is that something you can provision for a 3–5 day test window?
2) Can you confirm the JSONL sample schema precisely (an example line would help) — I want to be sure our export script maps fields correctly.
3) How long does a 1k-run typically take if you run all three model families?

Also looping in our procurement lead, Liam Park (liam.park@fincorp.com), for any quick questions on trial T&Cs.

Samira
Director, ML Ops
FinCorp

Hi Samira — happy to coordinate. Short answers:

1) Yes, we can provision a Dedicated eval pool for a 5-day window; we'll enable customer-managed KMS and set retention to 30 days by default unless you request shorter.
2) Example JSONL line (one line):
   {"id": "fc-0001", "input": "Customer: I was charged twice for my subscription...", "expected": "billing_duplicate_charge", "meta": {"region": "us-east-1", "source": "email"}}

3) Runtime: for 1k examples, running the three families in parallel typically completes within 6–10 hours depending on the batch profile (we'll provide a precise ETA after we see your token distribution).

If you approve, we can create a secure S3 bucket and a presigned upload link; alternatively, you can drop the redacted file into the Google Drive folder I shared.

I'll start a provisioning request as soon as you confirm Dedicated + KMS.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
